title: Testing Whether Sycophancy Persists After Constitutional AI / RLAIF Fine-Tuning

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if RLAIF reduces sycophancy durably, it offers a tractable fix for open-weight models. If it only reduces surface-level sycophancy, that directly informs the field that deeper interventions are needed.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires constructing a constitutional AI dataset, LoRA fine-tuning, and running DeceptionBench sycophancy scenarios. Fine-tuning is advanced for beginner CS students even with medium compute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The end-to-end pipeline of dataset creation, fine-tuning, and before/after evaluation is sustained effort. Each step (dataset, training, evaluation) is individually manageable but together stretches 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: The CAI/RLAIF methodology is established and has been applied to Llama 3-8B with model collapse concerns raised. DeceptionBench provides the evaluation framework. The combination of RLAIF fine-tuning + sycophancy-specific evaluation on open models is partially explored but a focused study with before/after DeceptionBench evaluation would add incremental value.

evidence: Constitutional AI (Anthropic, 2022) established the RLAIF methodology but did not specifically measure its effect on sycophancy reduction.
arXiv:2504.04918 'Constitution or Collapse? Exploring Constitutional AI with Llama 3-8B' tested CAI on open-weight models and found potential for model collapse with recursive self-training.
DeceptionBench (PKU-Alignment, 2025) provides a comprehensive benchmark including sycophantic misrepresentation scenarios with escalating pressure levels.
44 US state attorneys general (Dec 2025) demanded safeguards against sycophantic AI, noting RLHF-based training amplifies sycophancy.

The specific question of whether RLAIF/CAI fine-tuning durably reduces sycophancy on open-weight models has been partially explored (Llama 3-8B CAI study) but not comprehensively with DeceptionBench-style evaluation.
